crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Tax Structuring and Planning
children.blurb: Tax structuring and planning within AI accounting covers how businesses arrange entities, transactions, and financing to manage tax obligations across jurisdictions, with attention to transfer pricing, permanent establishment, and tax attributes of AI-related assets.

children.name: Transfer Pricing
children.blurb: Transfer pricing concerns the prices charged between related entities within a multinational group for goods, services, intangibles, and financing.

children.name: Research Credits from Engineering Records
children.blurb: Research credits from engineering records concern the use of technical documentation, version histories, test logs, and design notes to substantiate research and development tax credit claims.

children.name: Sales, Use and Value Added Tax
children.blurb: Sales tax, use tax, and value added tax are transaction taxes levied on goods and services, with sales tax charged at the point of sale, use tax owed on taxable purchases where sales tax was not collected, and VAT applied at each stage of production with credit for input tax.

children.name: Audit Defence and Controversy
children.blurb: Audit defence and controversy covers the work of preparing for, responding to, and resolving disputes with tax authorities over positions that involve AI systems, data, or automated decisions.

sections.body: This field covers how artificial intelligence systems and the companies that build them handle tax obligations across borders. It includes decisions about where income is recognized, how internal prices are set between related entities, and which jurisdictions can claim tax revenue. In practice, AI accountants now pull data from engineering logs, cloud usage records, and contract databases to support tax positions. They also classify transactions for sales tax, use tax, and value added tax in many countries. The work is not theoretical; it runs on the same records that software teams already produce. The site tracks 214 compliance and regulation pages, and many of them feed directly into this section.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The state of this work is uneven. Some parts, like calculating research credits from payroll and cloud compute logs, are now routine for companies with clean engineering records. Transfer pricing remains difficult because the value of a model or a dataset is not settled, and tax authorities disagree on how to split profit between countries. Indirect tax is partly solved for standard software sales, but AI services that mix human review, model access, and data storage still create classification disputes. Audit defence is reactive and often depends on how well a company kept its original evidence. The honest limit is that no software can guarantee a tax outcome, and the site's 146 active AI lawsuits show that many positions are still being tested.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The five pages in this section move from planning to proof. Tax Structuring and Planning is where a reader would start to see how an AI company chooses its legal entities and where it books revenue. Transfer Pricing then explains how related entities set prices for shared models, data, and engineering work, which is the core of cross border tax risk. Research Credits from Engineering Records shows how to turn commit logs, compute usage, and experiment notes into defensible credit claims. Sales, Use and Value Added Tax covers the transaction level rules that apply when AI products are sold or consumed. Audit Defence and Controversy is the last stop, where all the earlier records are used to answer questions from tax authorities, and together they form a chain from initial structure to final evidence.
